AT0098.title: Proxy Pool
AT0098.description: A proxy pool is a collection and scheduling system of proxy IPs used by black-gray industry actors to rotate egress IPs. It integrates large numbers of residential, datacenter, and tunneling proxy IPs, dynamically rotating and on-demand scheduling them to provide crawlers, mass-registration, and credential-stuffing tasks with a massive supply of usable egress IPs — evading IP-based rate limiting (A0004), IP blocklists (A0016-001), and proxy detection (A0038). A proxy pool typically provides IP health checks, automatic removal of dead IPs, geographic/carrier filtering, concurrent allocation, and session persistence. Residential proxies (real home-broadband ISP IPs) carry the highest reputation and are the hardest for proxy detection to block, making them the most valuable resource in a proxy pool; datacenter proxies are cheap but easy to detect; tunneling proxies achieve single-ingress, multi-egress rotation via dynamic forwarding. The proxy pool is core infrastructure for large-scale scraping and black-market automation, working with IP providers (TA0011) to form the black-market IP supply chain. Distinguish from AT0034 Risk IP: AT0034 is an IP flagged as risky by risk control (a risk-control perspective), whereas AT0098 is the tool/system that schedules an IP pool (an attack-tool perspective).
